blocking.title: The nuclear age makes the game crawl: from the first strikes (1949) the nuclear system takes 7.0 to 10.1 ms of a 9.7 to 12.8 ms tick in years 13 to 19 (69 to 79 %), one call a day of about 170 to 240 ms (max 436 ms), and still 3.4 ms (58 to 61 %) in years 20 and 21, pinned and alone; years 9 to 11, with warheads but no strike, ran 3 to 4 ms; in the browser at Max a year goes from 20 to 25 s to 129 to 216 s
blocking.fix: Profile which part of the daily `nuclear` call costs 170 to 240 ms once strikes have happened (it is cheap in years 9 to 11 with warheads but no strike, and falls by half by year 20, so look at state that strikes create and that decays: fallout, outrage, shock, grievance, taboo, or the target scoring they feed); hold the tick to its budget in the late game, not only in year 1.

blocking.title: The AI's nuclear use is not credible: its first use in history is the Soviet Union, the largest nation on earth, bombing the revolt statelet Free Van three times in two days at utility 0.01 to 0.39; warheads then fall one a day, three in a row on one spot (Pinsk and Kovel; Odense three times), on Paramaribo, Aden, Malabo and Las Palmas, and on land no one holds; struck at London for 1.37 million dead, the United Kingdom never hits back at the Soviet Union and its one bomb goes to Chungking; the United States builds 87 warheads over 30 years and never uses one, while the revolt statelet 'Free Liège II' (founded #138, holding Berlin) builds warheads and makes 11 strike decisions on Germany, France, the Netherlands and British India in 1955 and 1956
blocking.fix: No first use against a nation that cannot threaten the striker (no warheads, tiny, not near the capital); no second warhead on a spot already struck; targets on the front or the enemy's core, not distant colonies; retaliation at the nation that struck; a bar on bursts on land no one holds.
